findings.title: The Edge middleware's .vc-config.json does not declare envVarsInUse, so the passcode and secret will probably never reach process.env
findings.claim: The Build Output API's Edge Function config has an `envVarsInUse: string[]` field: the list of project env var names the function may use. VC_CONFIG is only `{ runtime: 'edge', entrypoint: 'index.js' }`. Next.js's adapter fills `envVarsInUse` for its own middleware. Without it, a prebuilt `_middleware.func` should be expected to see `process.env.FTLITE_PASSCODE` and `FTLITE_COOKIE_SECRET` as undefined. Every request would then get the fail-closed 503 'FTLite is not configured.' The plan knows this is uncertain but only defers it to Web-iii, with no fallback.
findings.evidence: plan L42 (the Edge fact lists only runtime and entrypoint); L45 ('check this at Web-iii's first deploy … a 503 "not configured" page means the env did not reach the middleware'); L661 `VC_CONFIG = { runtime: 'edge', entrypoint: 'index.js' }`; L669 writes it; L685 `checkWebOutput` requires exactly VC_CONFIG; L281 the middleware reads `process.env.FTLITE_PASSCODE` and `process.env.FTLITE_COOKIE_SECRET`; L256 returns 503 when either is missing.
findings.why: It fails closed, so nothing leaks. But Web-iii's first `deploy:web` would put the whole site behind a 503, and only a Build Output change and a new deploy fix it. This is a wrong Vercel layout under the review's rules, and it costs one line to fix now.
findings.fix: Set `VC_CONFIG = { runtime: 'edge', entrypoint: 'index.js', envVarsInUse: ['FTLITE_PASSCODE', 'FTLITE_COOKIE_SECRET'] }`; the check at L685 then requires it. Correct the fact at L42 and keep the 503 check at L45 as the Web-iii confirmation. Add one line to the gates.md owner steps (L848-L850): if the live page still answers 503 with both vars set, the vars are not reaching the middleware; check that they are set for Production and redeploy.

findings.title: Web Lock: the menu waits on the lock with no time limit, the lock is never released on pagehide, and a busy lock is never retried, so a reload can lock online play out
findings.claim: `startApp` awaits `acquireOnlineLock` before the store and menu exist, with no timeout. If `locks.request` ever fails to call back or settle, Single player never appears, which breaks spec §7.5's promise that Single player stays available. The lock is released only when the document is destroyed: Task 10's pagehide teardown never calls `lock.release()`. A busy lock is final for the tab's life (`ifAvailable: true`, one try). On a reload, the new document's request can race the old document's release and come back 'busy'. The reloaded tab then shows 'FTLite is already open in another tab', with online play off, until the next reload. No gate reloads a page: Task 11 closes the tab and reopens it.
findings.evidence: plan L1547-L1557 (one `ifAvailable` request, no timeout, no retry); L1656 `const lock … = web && configured ? await acquireOnlineLock(navigator.locks) : …`, before `createUiStore`; L1657 only a held lock creates the session; L2104-L2111 the pagehide teardown has no `lock.release()`; L2396-L2398 the gate closes and reopens and never calls `page.reload()`; spec L314.
findings.why: A reload is ordinary play: the update banner's 'reload' button (L1064), a stuck tab, or F5. Losing online play after a reload looks like a broken game, and an unbounded await sits in front of Single player.
findings.fix: (1) Wrap the acquisition in a 2 s `Promise.race`; on timeout, use `{ state: 'unavailable' }` and keep starting the app. (2) In Task 10's pagehide teardown, call `lock.state === 'held' && lock.release()` after `bridge?.dispose()`. (3) On 'busy', retry once with a waiting request, `locks.request(name, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1500) }, …)`, before showing ONE_TAB_TEXT, so a reload's old document has time to release. (4) Add a reload case to Task 11: reload the guest with `page.reload()` before Reconnect, or add a reload step, and assert that `__ftliteOnlineTest` exists afterwards.

findings.title: The origin-refused injection passes on any failure to reach the lobby, not only on the refused origin
findings.claim: The injection counts as 'failed for its named reason' when the first pairing's host either shows any online error or times out waiting for the lobby. A broken create path, a dead Worker, a service fault or a slow machine all match the same regex, so the run never proves that the service refused the page's Origin.
findings.evidence: plan L2469 (the injection only drops the preview origin from ALLOWED_ORIGINS); L2509-L2510 the regex `chromium-host lobby(: online error | timeout)`; L2374 `phase(h, 'lobby', 20000)` times out for any cause; services/signalling/src/index.ts:L63-L65 (a disallowed origin gets a 403 'forbidden' without CORS headers, which the page only sees as a network TypeError).
findings.why: Web-i's gate lesson (plan L30) is that 'a failure injection must fail for its named reason'. As written, this injection can pass while the real cause is something else.
findings.fix: In `createBrowserPlayer`, record `page.on('response')` and `page.on('requestfailed')` for the service origin. Playwright sees the 403 even when CORS hides it from page script. In inject mode, require a 403 on `POST /v2/rooms` whose request carried `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, and no 2xx create response, as well as the lobby failure. Without that 403, exit 2.

findings.title: The rehost step does not show that the mirror was written to, or read from, IndexedDB
findings.claim: `mirror.persistent` starts true and turns false only after a failed save. So `committed && persistent` is true before any IndexedDB write has finished. The guest rehosts in the same page that holds the mirror in memory. Rehost checks the in-memory `value.mirror.committed` against the service checkpoint. Nothing in the gate reads or reloads from IndexedDB, yet the report claims 'rehost from the IndexedDB mirror'.
findings.evidence: plan L2408 waits on `!!v.status.mirror.committed && v.status.mirror.persistent`; src/network/online/onlineMirrors.ts:L29 `persistent = true` at start, and L59-L60 (cleared only on a save failure); plan L2412 rehost in the same page; src/network/online/onlineSession.ts:L361-L366 (rehost uses the in-memory `value.mirror.committed` plus `getCheckpoint`); plan L2494 and L2536 claim 'rehost from the IndexedDB mirror'; spec L376.
findings.why: Spec §8 asks for rehost from the IndexedDB mirror. The browser's IndexedDB mirror path (fake-indexeddb in unit tests only) gets no end-to-end evidence across Chromium, Firefox and Electron.
findings.fix: After the host tab closes, close and reopen the guest page in the same context, then Multiplayer, Reconnect saved seat, wait for 'saved' with 'rehost', and click Rehost. The committed mirror can then only have come from IndexedDB. Also require `!v.status.mirror.localPending`. If that flow is not offered, read `mirror-v1` from IndexedDB with `page.evaluate` and check that its checkpoint sequence matches `status.mirror.committed` before rehosting.

findings.title: The Web-iii live checks never test the paid art or the game files, with or without the cookie
findings.claim: The owner's post-deploy check is only `curl -I` showing a 401 without the cookie and `no-store` on `/version.json`. Two of spec §5.3's requirements cannot be proved locally. One is that the Routing Middleware really runs in front of static files such as `/assets/paid/*` (the output check imports the bundle in Node). The other is that a `config.json` route header overrides Vercel's default static `Cache-Control` and gives `private`. Neither has a live check or a fallback.
findings.evidence: plan L850 (the curl check: 401 and version.json `no-store` only); L656-L660 (routes: middleware, then `private, no-cache`, then version.json `no-store`); L50 (W-2); L682-L713 (`checkWebOutput` runs the bundle in Node, not Vercel's router); spec L239 and L249.
findings.why: A deploy where `/assets/paid/x.png` answers 200 without the cookie would expose the paid art, which is P0 territory. Nothing scheduled would catch it.
findings.fix: Extend gates.md step 5 (L850) with: without the cookie, `curl -I https://<project>.vercel.app/assets/paid/<a real file>` and `/assets/authorityWorker.js` answer 401. With the cookie (`-b ftlite_pass=…` from a browser sign-in), `/`, `/assets/authorityWorker.js` and the paid file answer 200 with `cache-control: private, no-cache`, and `/version.json` answers with `no-store`. Add the same checks to `scripts/web/live-smoke.ts` in Web-iii, and state that the first deploy is rolled back if any of them fails.

findings.title: When the lock is 'unavailable' in a supported browser, the Multiplayer screen shows the wrong text
findings.claim: If `locks.request` rejects (for example a SecurityError) in a browser that passed the support check, `onlineConfig` becomes null and `onlineBlocked` stays null. The Multiplayer screen then says 'Online play needs a configured local service. Single player is available.'
findings.evidence: plan L1656-L1661 (`onlineBlocked` is set only for 'busy'); src/renderer/src/ui/menuState.ts:L52 and L83-L86 (`availabilityText` falls back to the online-disabled text).
findings.why: Players are not running a 'local service'. The text sends them in the wrong direction.
findings.fix: Set `onlineBlocked: lock.state === 'busy' ? ONE_TAB_TEXT : lock.state === 'unavailable' && configured ? UNSUPPORTED_TEXT : null`, or give the unavailable case its own short text.

findings.title: In the browser, Settings still says F11 toggles fullscreen, but F11 is the browser's own fullscreen and the API cannot see it
findings.claim: Settings prints '<FULLSCREEN_KEY> also toggles fullscreen.' F11 in a browser is browser-chrome fullscreen: `document.fullscreenElement` stays null, so the toggle reads 'Off' while the window is fullscreen. W-7 and §7.1 leave F11 to the browser.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/ui/menu/Settings.tsx:L34-L36; plan L1305 (`isOn` reads `fullscreenElement`); L1354 and L1360-L1361 (the browser fullscreen deps); spec L286.
findings.why: The label disagrees with what the player sees after pressing F11.
findings.fix: Add `web` to the browser slice, or pass a flag, and in the browser hide the F11 note or replace it with a line saying F11 is the browser's own fullscreen.

verified: Task 1 passcode: the cookie MAC is checked with `crypto.subtle.verify` (constant time, plan L223), after a strict `^\d{1,12}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$` format check. The expiry must satisfy `now < expiry <= now+30d` (L220), so expired cookies, cookies expiring exactly now and future-forged ones are refused (test L151-L167). The passcode compare hashes both sides with SHA-256 and XORs them (L233-L237). A failed POST really sleeps 1 s through env.sleep, which is setTimeout in middleware.ts (L265, L282). The secret is decoded with `atob` and must be at least 32 bytes, otherwise 503 (L204-L207). Without a valid cookie every path answers the 401 page, including `/assets/paid/*`, `/version.json`, `/assets/authorityWorker.js` and `/__pass` (L268-L269, test PATHS L124).

Task 2: `resolveOnlineConfig` and `validatePageOnlineConfig` exist with the shapes the plan assumes (src/shared/onlineConfig.ts:L6-L18, L42-L53). The refusal cases (trailing slash, path, userinfo, a leading space, http in production) all fail through the raw regex or the `baseUrl !== origin` check. W-1 is needed because `packaged: true` forbids test fields (onlineConfig.ts:L48), and the plan states and justifies it.

Task 2: `computeBuildInfo`, `readSimVersion` (build/buildInfo.ts:L8, L21) and `computeContentDigest` (build/contentDigest.ts:L7) match. The new electron.vite.config.ts matches the current file (L1-L31) except for the shared renderer settings. `__FTLITE_WEB_CONFIG__` is declared beside `__FTLITE_BUILD__` in src/renderer/src/net/env.d.ts, which tsconfig.node.json L8 includes, and is defined in vitest.config.ts L7. Build info is deterministic for one tree, so the banner cannot fire on its own build.
No file in the content digest manifest is touched: build/contentDigest.ts:L12-L16 does not list net/duelRecord.ts, recordStore.ts or main.ts.

Task 5 store and actions: `UiStoreInit`, `createUiStore` (store.ts:L10-L23), `UiActionDeps.quit` and the returned `quit()` (actions.ts:L19, L91), and Menu's `playing` and its `single` early return (Menu.tsx:L19-L36) all match the edits. The banner text is `New version: reload`. `isPlaying` matches menuState.ts:L67.

Task 6: `PRESS_CODES`, `FREQ_CODES`, `WEAPON_CODES`, `MOVE_CODES`, `INTERACT_HELD` and `PING_CODE` (app/duel/input.ts:L11-L26) and `SECTOR_KEYS` (input/sources.ts:L4) exist. The duel keyboards listen on window (duelMode.ts:L54, onlineDuel.ts:L86), so Task 7's synthetic Escape dispatched on window reaches them.

Task 7: the three spec §7.2 conditions are implemented. The page-exit flag uses a 1000 ms window that also covers a fullscreenchange arriving after `exitFullscreen` resolves, and a failed exit resets it. A match must be running. The 100 ms Escape dedupe is a strict `>` (plan L1312). A locked exit never counts as a press. `requestFullscreen` is called synchronously inside the Settings click (actions.ts:L143-L146), so the user gesture holds.

Task 8: `PageOnlineDeps`, `createPageOnline` and its `action()` match pageSession.ts:L33-L41 and L89-L95. `OnlineSessionOwner` (onlineSession.ts:L39-L46) and `OnlineLifecycle` (lifecycle.ts:L4) match the test doubles. The Home, Multiplayer and Settings first lines match the files.

Task 9: the 1→2 IndexedDB upgrade creates only the missing stores, so `records` (seat-v1, mirror-v1) survives both 0→2 and 1→2. The existing v1 code closes its connection on `onversionchange` (recordStore.ts:L29). The new openers set the same handler. Electron's page uses the same database through `createIndexedDbRecordStore`.

Task 10: Web-i's own pagehide listener, registered first inside createPageOnline (pageSession.ts:L98-L99), still runs `releaseForUnload` before main's teardown. The Electron close path is unchanged: `prepareExit` then detach (pageSession.ts:L132), and main ignores `will-prevent-unload` (src/main/index.ts:L49). The prompt is web-only. The persisted pagehide is still handled by the clock-jump lifecycle (lifecycle.ts:L39-L41).

Task 11 reuses the Web-i gates correctly. `buildDuelObservers` writes observer.js, page-probe.js and utility.cjs (online-observer-build.ts:L18-L21). `startLocalRuntime(dir, { allowedOrigins })` matches local-runtime.ts:L8. Ports are counted through `onlineProbe.openPorts`, armed on the first click, and Worker exits are counted from `terminate()` only (page-probe.ts:L28-L34, L84). Every page call is bounded. The duel walk routes, the `results`/`present`/`pauseReason` fields and the Escape resume mirror duel-app-smoke.ts:L76-L95 and L183-L194.
W-2 `private, no-cache` keeps spec §5.3's `private` and adds revalidation, so it is consistent with the spec. W-4 matches §5.4 (no poll or banner in Single player) and §7.6.
